mission: LÉLU 2.1 — geometry fidelity and mathematical validation
observed: The 2.0 report claimed a more uniform hair root layout. The same comparison re-read from the published files reports CV 1.3446 at n=928 against 0.6434 at n=1350 — 11 verdicts, 3 warnings.
studied: Sampling-uniformity statistics and how the coefficient of variation depends on sample count.
question: Do the 2.0 uniformity claims survive an independent re-measurement?
hypothesis: The golden layout is more uniform than the baseline on every published metric.
method: Re-read every published value from its own artefact path (no transcription), recompute the winner, and refuse a claim when the two sides were measured at different sample counts or when the metric does not describe both layouts.
results: Audit ok=true with 3 warnings. The hair CV comparison is confounded (928 vs 1350). Divergence and radial exponent are not applicable to concentric rings, so they cannot be wins. The 2.0 ringlet was mis-parameterised: growth was 1.09×/turn, not φ.

evidence.note: every verdict, with its source path and sample count
eight guard tests, one per way a claim can lie

learned: Three of the 2.0 claims were artefacts of unequal sample counts or of applying a disc metric to a ring layout. The comparison that survives is the equal-n one: 0.3925 → 0.0968 at n=800, a 75.3% reduction.
limitations: The audit re-reads files; it cannot repair an experiment that was never run at equal n.
Blueprint: the original 2.0 renders were not regenerated, only their measurements re-checked.
applications: Any future uniformity claim must name the sample count on both sides.
The audit is re-runnable and gates the report.
nextQuestions: How many other published numbers were computed at unequal sample counts?
Does the equal-n result hold on the garment and disc surfaces too?
answers: Do the 2.0 uniformity claims survive an independent re-measurement?

assumptions.statement: published metrics were comparable across variants
the golden ringlet used φ per turn
